sentences.span: AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: BofA's equity derivatives team explicitly names the bond-market-vs-equity-market disconnect the 'AI put'.

sentences.span: in a market with "a relatively fixed supply of attention", macro risk "is struggling to compete for attention with the growth potential of AI narratives." AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying
sentences.why: Matches the mechanism BofA describes almost verbatim: fixed attention supply, AI narratives winning attention from macro risk, resulting dip-buying.

sentences.span: For the bears... For the bulls... As Rich Privorotsky pointed out to me
sentences.why: Framing sentence; GS's own note stages bear/bull cases on what rates mean, and BofA's AI-put note takes a distinct, more sanguine stance on the same bond-market stress, supporting a genuine split between two tier-1 desks.

sentences.span: one year ago, the forward P/E of S&P was 23x; today it's 19x... S&P has been mired in a tyrannical range trade around the 7700 level
sentences.why: Exact match on both the P/E compression (23x to 19x) and the S&P range near 7700.

sentences.span: when 10-year notes back up 2 standard deviations in one month's time, S&P usually begins to show some strain... that rule of thumb was just triggered
sentences.why: Pasquariello's 'speed limit' rule is framed around the pace/magnitude of the yield move (2 std-dev in a month), not an absolute yield level, matching the sentence's claim.

sentences.span: I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here.
sentences.why: Direct quote of Privorotsky's three-item checklist, matching the sentence's three items exactly.

sentences.span: France had its own idiosyncratic story... but the initial catalyst for this week's front-end-led widening was deleveraging... Europe might not be able to sustain these levels of rates
sentences.why: Supports France as the place where the global rate repricing produced a visible break (sovereign spread widening).

sentences.span: Fair value for the 10y OAT-Bund spread stands at 100-110bp... We cut our French growth forecasts again, to 0.3% and 0.6% for this year and next
sentences.why: Exact match on both the BofA fair-value spread range and the French growth forecast cuts.

sentences.span: does Europe reap enough of the benefits from a growth perspective to be fine too? Or does it just pay the price of a higher cost of funding?... growth is just ~1%
sentences.why: Matches Goldman's framing of the open question almost verbatim, including the ~1% European growth figure.

sentences.span: 2026 projected hyperscaler issuance of $250bn... with most of this year's funding ($230bn) completed. 2027 Hyperscaler forecasts of $420bn... We recently raised our top-down forecast... $420bn (vs. $400bn previously)... 35% of 2027's hyperscaler CapEx spending will be debt funded
sentences.why: All four figures ($250bn, $230bn, $420bn vs $400bn, 35%) match Goldman's credit strategists exactly.

sentences.span: The junkiest junk is leading credit losses but the rest of high yield is starting to catch up.
sentences.why: Framing sentence supported by the CCC/Oracle stress detailed immediately after in the same source.

sentences.span: 1,007 bps, the first time above 1,000 since the March 2023 bank scare... Its 5Y CDS hit a record ~227 bps, its 2056 bonds yield above 8%
sentences.why: Exact match on the CCC spread level/date reference and Oracle's CDS and bond yield figures.

sentences.span: Given the still elevated net Asset Manager position, expect ongoing challenges until yields convincingly reverse.
sentences.why: GS names a reversal in yields as the condition for relief; paired with BofA's technical note (18431) framing the real-yield breakout as the parallel risk driver, both desks point to the same real-yield mechanism as the trigger.

sentences.span: Oil prices extended the week's rise, with Brent above $102 by late Friday
sentences.why: Exact match for Brent above $102 late Friday, paired with Goldman's 23.6mb/d Persian Gulf export estimate and 'roughly balanced' market read from the Crook note.

sentences.span: our base case that Brent prices moderate to $85/bbl by year-end and to $80 in 2027
sentences.why: Matches Goldman's Brent base case exactly; the G7 100mb release is confirmed in the companion Evans commodity note (18703: 'the G7 agreed on Friday to release 100mb of crude and distillate').
